It reproduces the SED within 0.07 dex and the total- and polarized-intensity profiles; the fractional polarization peaks at 15% at 1.7 arcsec (observed: 14%). The rising surface density of the ring produces the polarized-intensity plateau, and 0.5 $μ$m grains at its outer edge the decline beyond 2 arcsec; grains of $\gtrsim 0.7$ $μ$m are excluded. A thin disk of large grains suggests a settled mid-plane. Stellar temperatures of 7000-8500 K fit equally well. Of the total extinction ($A_V \approx 6.9$ mag), 5 mag is interstellar. Most of the $7.4 \times 10^{-2}$ $M_\odot$ of dust is equatorial; the envelope implies a mass-loss rate of $\approx 10^{-5}$-$10^{-4}$ ($ψ$/100) $M_\odot$ yr$^{-1}$. Because equatorial dust redirects starlight poleward, the pole-on SED overestimates the luminosity by $\approx 1.5$; at the Gaia distance, $L_\star \approx 3.3 \times 10^5$ $L_\odot$. Subtracting a scaled stellar PSF removes most of the nebular light within $\approx 1$ arcsec.

entries.title: The shape and velocity of black hole coronas
entries.abstract: The first highly significant detection of the polarization of the X-rays from the Black Hole X-ray Binary Cygnus X-1 revealed surprisingly strong polarization parallel to its radio jet. The observation is now commonly interpreted as resulting from the Comptonization of some lower frequency seed photons in a laterally extended corona. The emitting plasma is likely moving along the jet axis with a sizable fraction beta of the speed of light, amplifying the polarization degree. In this letter we address the question of how laterally extended the corona actually needs to be to account for the observations, and we calculate the required outflow velocities of velocity-stratified coronas as a function of the stationary-frame aspect ratio h=H/2R of cylindrical coronas of height H and radius R. We find that models with h lesser equal 0.8 and beta=0.5-0.9 at the top of the corona can give both the observed photon index of Gamma=1.6 and the observed 4% polarization parallel to the symmetry axis. We do not find suitable solutions for larger h. Given the constraints on h, we discuss the likely size of the corona, emphasizing that compact coronas close to the black hole are preferred as they can tap more efficiently into the gravitational energy and the rotational energy of the black hole, and are less exposed to their own emission reprocessed in the optically thick portion of the accretion flow.

entries.title: A Poisson-bracket operator for Hamiltonian separability: intrinsic geometry and exact defects
entries.abstract: Additive separation of the Hamilton-Jacobi equation depends on the Hamiltonian and on the canonical variables, and this paper introduces a five-input Poisson-bracket operator whose values on canonical pairs reproduce the Levi-Civita separability expressions. On a symplectic product structure its off-diagonal values are intrinsic, since they equal a symplectic pairing of the sector Hamiltonian fields and measure the Frobenius obstruction of a Lagrangian distribution, and their vanishing yields a local separation theorem. Because the operator is cubic in the Hamiltonian, its perturbation expansion is exact and defines a linearised separability operator and a defect functional. For Hamiltonians with a cyclic angle, the linearised operator divided by the squared rotor frequency is an angle derivative of the Melnikov integrand, so that the defect integrated along a homoclinic orbit decides the first-order splitting of the separatrix. Closed-form defects are obtained for the polar-nodal normal forms of satellite theory and, through a covariance of the operator on level sets, for Kerr geodesics. Used for coordinate selection, the defect singles out the separating focal distance of the Euler two-centre problem as its unique nondegenerate minimum, and for axisymmetric potentials it shows that the prescriptions of Sanders and Vasiliev are two weightings of the same Stäckel residual. The residual selector and Binney's shell-orbit fit improve both actions over the median prescription for 48 and 50 of 50 orbits in a flattened logarithmic potential, whereas the operator selector lowers the 90th-percentile action spread of 50 orbits in a Miyamoto-Nagai potential from 2.90% to 0.91%.

entries.title: Could globular clusters in the vicinity of the galactic centre have contributed stars to the nuclear star cluster in the past?
entries.abstract: The results of direct N-body simulations of three Milky Way bulge globular clusters - Terzan 2, Terzan 4, and Terzan 5 - evolving in a time-varying galactic potential derived from the IllustrisTNG-100 cosmological database over 8 Gyr are presented. Incorporating full stellar evolution and compact remnant formation, we quantify the probability and efficiency of stellar accretion onto the Galactic nuclear star cluster (NSC) during close pericentre passages of these three clusters. To parametrize the effect of dynamical friction in the dense central environment, we introduce a velocity reduction factor (Vred) ranging from 1.00 to 0.10. It was found that all three clusters contribute stars to the NSC even in the absence of velocity reduction, with a combined bound stellar count of 730 stars and a total accreted mass of 278 Msol at Vred = 1.00, growing to 5420 stars and 1175 Msol at Vred = 0.10. Terzan 4 is the dominant contributor across all velocity reduction factors, reflecting its more frequent and closer pericentre passages near the Galactic centre. The mass distribution of accreted stars reveals a bimodal structure: a low-mass component below 1 Msol whose capture is independent of Vred, and a prominent high-mass tail extending to 20 Msol corresponding to neutron stars and black holes, which grows with decreasing Vred. Notably, Terzan 4 is the only cluster for which white dwarfs are also captured by the NSC at every Vred value. Our results suggest that the Terzan family represents a more significant source of compact remnants for the Galactic NSC than previously studied clusters, while confirming that tidal stripping of surviving globular clusters alone cannot account for the total NSC mass.

entries.title: Dust in cold and warm dark matter in a suite of zoom-in simulations of Milky Way analogues
entries.abstract: We use a suite of hydrodynamical zoom-in simulations of Milky Way analogues to investigate how previously identified trends in dust properties of galaxies can be utilised to infer the underlying dark matter model. We use a sample of 24 comparison simulations comparing a cold dark matter (CDM) and 3.5 keV warm dark matter (WDM) particle, primarily using a dust-to-metals (DTM) ratio to post-process the dust in the simulation, with alternative methods explored. We find a preference for higher dust masses in CDM over WDM, with a median increase of 6.6 per cent in the CDM sample at redshift $z=0$, and with a peak median difference of 25 per cent at $z\approx0.25$. Both CDM and WDM samples are highly concentrated, with approximately 90 per cent of the dust located in the inner region of the halo, though slightly higher in CDM. Contrary to previous work, we find that the Gini coefficient does not consistently show a difference in comparisons of dark matter models, with differences primarily driven by high sensitivity to the unique structure of individual haloes. Finally, we conduct an analysis of some common dust scaling relations, finding that the differences between the two samples in the dust-to-stellar mass and dust-to-SFR functions do not constitute a statistically significant difference at $z=0$ with any dust production mechanism. However, at redshifts where the difference in dust mass is greatest, the alternative dust production methods show larger separations between CDM and WDM samples in total mass and scaling relations.

entries.title: Enhanced Mid-Photospheric Heating Around a Solar Pore
entries.abstract: We present depth-stratified atmospheric reconstructions of a solar pore observed with the Sunrise Chromospheric Infrared SpectroPolarimeter (SCIP) aboard \textsc{Sunrise~iii}. Using spatially coupled NLTE spectropolarimetric inversions, we characterize the thermal, magnetic, and velocity structure of the pore and its surroundings from the photosphere to the chromosphere over approximately two hours. The inversions recover the canonical photospheric properties of pores: a cool umbra with strong magnetic fields dominated by the vertical component. Most photospheric velocities are subsonic, but localized downflows near the pore boundary reach transonic or potentially supersonic values around $\logτ_{500}=0$. At higher atmospheric layers, the thermal contrast between the pore and its surroundings decreases substantially. We also detect localized mid-photospheric temperature enhancements forming a patchy, ring-like structure in the wings of the Ca\,{\sc ii} 8542\,Å line, without a clear continuum counterpart. The temperature excess reaches approximately $300$\,K and corresponds to an excess thermal-energy density of up to $170$\,J\,m$^{-3}$. These regions coincide with an enhanced transverse magnetic-field component and the expanding magnetic canopy surrounding the pore. The structure is detected in all three rasters, although the cadence does not establish whether individual patches persist or repeatedly re-form. While the heating mechanism cannot be uniquely identified, the inferred magnetic topology supports an association with processes operating in the expanding canopy. These results demonstrate the value of pores for investigating the coupling between magnetic topology, convection, and atmospheric energy transport.

entries.title: An assessment of the Weak Field Approximation
entries.abstract: The Weak Field Approximation (WFA) is widely used to infer magnetic fields from solar spectropolarimetric observations. However, its validity and sensitivity to atmospheric conditions are not fully understood. We investigate the reliability and limitations of the WFA using Generalized Response Functions (GRFs), which quantify the sensitivity of the inferred magnetic field to atmospheric perturbations. We derive analytical expressions for the WFA GRFs and compute them from synthetic Stokes profiles generated with the SIR and DeSIRe radiative transfer codes. We consider photospheric and chromospheric lines under different magnetic field strengths and inclinations. The inferred magnetic field depends on the atmospheric structure, field inclination, and wavelength range. For photospheric lines, the WFA increasingly departs from the actual field strength well before reaching the saturation value, due to the loss of linearity between Stokes V, Q, and U and the intensity profile derivatives. The transverse-field inference is particularly sensitive to the wavelength range, with line wings providing more reliable estimates. For chromospheric lines, the core and wings probe different atmospheric layers, with the wings providing reliable estimates of the photospheric field. The WFA has a more limited range of validity than commonly assumed. Its reliability depends on field strength, inclination, and wavelength selection, particularly for the transverse component. Chromospheric line wings can also provide useful information on the photospheric magnetic field. These findings support the original perturbative formulation of the WFA.

entries.title: Intermediate-redshift ultra-luminous infrared galaxies as transitioning objects between main sequence and starburst galaxies
entries.abstract: With their star formation efficiencies (SFE) and star formation rates (SFR) falling between normal star-forming galaxies and starbursts (SBs), ultra-luminous infrared galaxies (ULIRGs) at intermediate redshifts ($0.2<z<1$) have been postulated to be good probes of galaxies transitioning between these two regimes. Here, we present new Atacama Large Millimetre Array (ALMA) observations of a representative sample of 22 ULIRGs at redshifts $0.46<z<0.81$ evenly distributed across dust temperature ranges of $25<T_{\rm dust}<50~K$ and spanning infrared luminosities of $10^{12.0}<L_\text{IR}<10^{12.7}~L_\odot$. We detected CO(2-1) emission in 14 of these galaxies (64%). The SFE of these 14 targets are all similar, corresponding to depletion timescales on the order of hundreds of Myr. By employing two different versions of the main sequence relation of galaxies -- one based on the specific SFR (sSFR) and one based on directly observable parameters (CO and IR luminosities) -- we statistically confirm that the present sample of intermediate redshift ULIRGs indeed lies in the transitional region between MS and SB galaxies. In addition, we establish that the SFE of our sample of ULIRGs is a strong indicator of the position of a galaxy relative to the MS and the SB branches. Based on the observed morphologies and star-forming properties, we suggest that minor mergers provide a viable mechanism for temporarily enhancing the SFR and SFE of intermediate-redshift ULIRGs, although other evolutionary phases and pathways cannot be excluded.

entries.title: SuperWIMPs in the Kination Era: Imprints on $N_{\rm eff}$ and CMB Spectral Distortions
entries.abstract: We investigate how the late-time decays of unstable particles into dark matter and neutrinos can leave measurable imprints on both cosmological observables and collider experiments. We study this mechanism within the scotogenic model, where the lightest singlet fermion $N_1$ serves as the dark matter candidate and is produced via the late decay of the lightest inert doublet scalar via the superWIMP mechanism. By incorporating a kination-dominated era in the early Universe, the altered expansion rate allows to match the observed $N_1$ relic density in parameter regions that would be underabundant in standard cosmology. The energy exchange between the injected neutrinos and photons resulting from the late-time decay can produce CMB spectral $μ$-distortions, detectable shifts in the effective number of relativistic species $N_{\rm eff}$, or both simultaneously. Concentrating on the lightest component of inert doublet scalars with masses between $200$ and $500~\text{GeV}$, we find that these cosmological signals are accompanied by complementary signatures accessible at the LHC. Although our analysis is derived within the scotogenic framework, our findings apply more broadly to scenarios in which the unstable particle undergoes late-time out-of-equilibrium decay to produce dark matter and non-thermal neutrinos, offering how future CMB measurements and collider searches can jointly probe dark matter production and the early Universe's thermal history.

entries.title: Measurement of the Neutrino Spectrum along the Galactic Plane with IceCube
entries.abstract: We present the first measurement of the variation of the high-energy neutrino flux along the Galactic plane using 10 years of neutrino-induced particle-shower data from the IceCube Neutrino Observatory. In this Letter, we fit both the neutrino flux normalization and the spectral index, in multiple regions along the plane, independent of model expectations. The neutrino flux per solid angle in the inner Galactic region ($\vert l\vert< 30^{\circ}, \vert b\vert < 8^{\circ}$) is approximately five times higher than in the outer Galactic plane ($\vert l\vert>60^{\circ}, \vert b\vert < 8^{\circ}$) at $E_ν=5\mathrm{TeV}$. The spectral indices in the inner and outer region are $γ=2.76^{+0.18}_{-0.15}$ and $γ= 3.13^{+0.57}_{-0.37}$, respectively. Additionally, we compare the same region of Galactic emission measured in $\mathrm{TeV}$ gamma rays by LHAASO ($15^{\circ}<l<125^{\circ}$) to neutrinos, and conclude that the measurements are compatible within uncertainties, under the assumption of hadronic gamma-ray production.

entries.title: A Comprehensive Analysis of the H$α$ Luminosity Functions at $z\sim 1.3$ and $z\sim 2.0$ in the CANUCS Lensing Fields with JWST NIRISS
entries.abstract: We present H$α$ luminosity function (LF) measurements at redshifts $z\sim1.3$ and $z\sim2.0$. We adopt JWST grism data in five lensing cluster fields and their parallel fields from the CANUCS program: ABELL-370, MACS-J0416, MACS-J0417, MACS-J1149, MACS-J1423. Based on emission lines spectroscopically identified in the F115W, F150W and F200W filters, our final sample consists of 762 H$α$ emitters, including 433 at $1.1<z<1.5$ and 329 at $1.8<z<2.2$. Through detailed effective volume and completeness analysis for each source, we construct the H$α$ LF in two redshift bins. Thanks to the sensitivity of NIRISS WFSS and gravitational lensing magnification, our sample reaches intrinsic H$α$ luminosities down to $L_{\rm Hα}\sim10^{40.6}~\rm erg~s^{-1}$ at $z\sim1.3$ and $L_{\rm Hα}\sim10^{41}~\rm erg~s^{-1}$ at $z\sim2.0$ with completeness larger than 80\%. The larger survey volume and coverage of multiple independent sightlines help mitigate cosmic variance. After accounting for cosmic variance, we constrain the faint-end slopes to be $α_{\mathrm{H}α}=-1.51^{+0.06}_{-0.04}$ at $z\sim1.3$ and $-1.42^{+0.09}_{-0.06}$ at $z\sim2.0$, indicating a mild evolution between the two redshift bins. We find a negligible contribution from bright active galactic nuclei in our sample. We estimate integrated cosmic star formation rate densities of $0.103^{+0.008}_{-0.007}~M_{\odot}~\rm yr^{-1}~Mpc^{-3}$ at $z\sim1.3$ and $0.149^{+0.016}_{-0.013}~M_{\odot}~\rm yr^{-1}~Mpc^{-3}$ at $z\sim2.0$. The emission-line samples presented here will enable further detailed studies of galaxy properties including metallicities. The methodology presented here can be readily applicable to other JWST slitless spectroscopic datasets and future wide-field slitless surveys, including those from Euclid, Roman, and the Chinese Space Station Telescope.

entries.title: Depth of Maximum of EAS and Mean Mass Composition of Primary CRs from the Spatial and Temporal Distribution of Cherenkov Light According to TAIGA-HiSCORE Data
entries.abstract: We present the dependence of the depth of maximum of extensive air showers (EAS), $X_{\max}$, on the energy of the primary particle, as determined from data recorded with the wide-angle Cherenkov array TAIGA-HiSCORE during the 2021--2025 observation seasons. The reconstruction of $X_{\max}$ from the experimental data uses relations obtained from EAS simulations: the dependence on the steepness of the Cherenkov light lateral distribution function ($P$-method) and on the full width at half maximum of the Cherenkov light pulse ($τ$-method). The reconstructed $X_{\max}$ values are converted into the mean logarithmic mass $\langle\ln A\rangle$, which characterizes the primary cosmic-ray mass composition. The results are compared with measurements from Tunka-133 (2017), the Pierre Auger Observatory (2019), LHAASO (2024), TALE (2026), and other experiments.

entries.title: Reabsorbed Urca neutrinos suppress bulk-viscous damping of neutron star merger oscillations
entries.abstract: Reabsorption of Urca neutrinos suppresses the bulk-viscous damping predicted for neutron star merger oscillations. Below the direct-Urca threshold the capture neutrinos have mean energies of 19-46 MeV and are absorbed within metres. An energy-resolved kinetic treatment gives 2.7 s for a 1-kHz, 10-km oscillation at nuclear density and 4 MeV, against 19 ms for freely escaping neutrinos. It holds across the sampled states, three equations of state and the rate variations, with nearly frozen composition. This absorption is present in full-kinematics rates and absent from elastic opacity tables.

entries.title: Zeeman-Doppler imaging of early-type stars. Testing Stokes parameter inversions with theoretical magnetohydrodynamic models
entries.abstract: Zeeman-Doppler imaging (ZDI) is widely used to reconstruct magnetic fields in early-type stars from time-series spectropolarimetric observations, yet its accuracy has not been systematically validated against physically self-consistent, complex magnetic field models. We aim to assess the reliability and limitations of modern ZDI techniques applied to fossil fields of early-type stars. We generated synthetic spectropolarimetric data from three-dimensional magnetohydrodynamic (MHD) simulations of fossil magnetic fields. The resulting Stokes profiles - individual lines and least-squares deconvolved (LSD) profiles - were inverted with contemporary ZDI codes using Stokes IQUV and IV data. We compared the reconstructed maps with the input MHD surface fields and quantified deviations in field strength, vector orientation, and harmonic energy decomposition. For Stokes IQUV inversions, ZDI recovers field vector components and strength with better than 10% accuracy, while Stokes IV inversions degrade to 15-20% for the most complex geometries. The field inclination is recovered to within 10 deg, with errors increasing to 15-20 deg in the same cases. Full Stokes inversions reproduce poloidal and toroidal energies to within a few percentage points. LSD-based inversions yield accuracy comparable to, and sometimes better than, that achieved with ZDI using individual Fe II lines. Imposing a current-free poloidal constraint, which the input field satisfies, only helps where the unconstrained Stokes IV inversion performs poorly. Cross-talk between magnetic and abundance reconstructions is weak, with spurious inhomogeneities at or below 0.1 dex on average. Modern ZDI robustly reconstructs fossil magnetic fields in early-type stars, including their smaller-scale non-dipolar features, particularly when full Stokes information is available.

entries.title: Parker Solar Probe Flies Through the Sun's Magnetic Poles Near 10 Solar Radii
entries.abstract: During the peak of the Sun's magnetic cycle, the solar corona can be complex and dominated by dynamics, while hidden below, the dipole component of the its photospheric magnetic field steadily reverses with respect to the rotational axis. Here, we use Parker Solar Probe (\emph{Parker}) data from two of its closest approaches in mid-2025 to show that the large-scale field at solar maximum resembled a simple tilted dipole. Similar to how Ulysses provided a complete scan of the solar rotation-aligned dipole at solar minimum, \emph{Parker} sampled the full range of magneto-latitudes, probing both magnetic poles below the Alfvén surface. Concurrent in situ data at larger distances reveal that both hemispheres contain solar wind with asymptotic speeds near 800 km s-1, yielding a picture similar to the Ulysses latitude scans but now in the equator near solar maximum. This contrasts with the disordered structure observed by Ulysses during its solar maximum latitude scan, which we attribute to the long timescale of data collection. Overall, we find the coronal field is organized as a dipole, but the fast solar wind streams are deformed by non-dipolar substructure: the positive dipole axis is aligned with one coronal hole, the negative centers over a pseudostreamer, and significant mass flux enhancements are observed at magnetic separatrixes. Our measurements suggest that even at solar maximum, the solar corona can still exhibit structure nearly as ordered as solar minimum. Moreover, by sampling rapidly and close to the Sun, the detailed imprint of source region structure can be determined in the solar wind.

entries.title: Revisiting the Einstein Cross with X-shooter spectra: New estimates of accretion disk parameters and broad emission line profiles from microlensing
entries.abstract: We present a spectroscopic study of the lensed quasar Q2237+0305, the Einstein Cross, assessing the best wavelength coverage to date with the X-shooter instrument (from $3000$ to $20000$ $\mathring{A}$), and thus improving the available spectroscopic data for this system. Using as a reference the characteristic emission lines for each quasar macro-image, we estimate the chromatic microlensing effect between pairs of images and calculate the extinction curve, confirming no significant differences between spectra $C$ and $A$ caused by extinction in the lens galaxy. In addition, we model the accretion disk characterized by a temperature profile with logarithmic slope $1/p$ and size $r_{s}$, assuming a thin-disk model with a power-law function of the form $r_{s}$ $\propto$ $λ^{p}$. To do this, we calculated a set of three chromatic microlensing measurements compiling previous estimates from the literature to test the wavelength dependence. This temperature profile was also compared to the canonical thin-disk model with $p=4/3$. Finally, we estimated the likelihood between the disk model and the observed data collected from multiple epochs through mock microlensing magnification maps and determined the probability density functions of each parameter from a Bayesian analysis. As a result, our estimated values for the accretion disk size and its exponential index are $r_{s}=4.9^{+2.3}_{-2.6}$ $\sqrt{M/0.3M_{\odot}}$ (lt-day) and $p=0.77^{+0.47}_{-0.28}$, respectively, reinforcing a departure from the standard accretion disk model ($ T \propto r_s^{-3/4}$).

entries.title: The Connection between Halo Assembly History and the Stellar Distribution II: A Radially Stratified Fossil Record of Past Halo Mass
entries.abstract: The spatial stellar distribution in massive central galaxies preserves a stratified fossil record of their host halos' assembly history. Using a halo-mass-complete sample from the IllustrisTNG-300 hydrodynamical simulation at $z=0.4$, we quantify this connection with two diagnostics. The fossil correlation $\tildeρ(z)$ measures how strongly a present-day galaxy property retains information about the progenitor halo mass at each redshift. The rank retention fraction $f_{\rm ret}(z)$ measures how many halos selected by that property today were among the most massive halos at each epoch. The central stellar mass at different galactocentric radii exhibits non-monotonic fossil correlations with past halo mass, peaking at intermediate redshifts that systematically shift from $z\sim1$ in the inner regions to $z\sim0.7$ in the outer stellar halos. These peak redshifts are robust from group to cluster scales. Partial correlations with halo accretion rate show that each peak marks the end of the epoch when that component's buildup was sensitive to halo accretion. The rank retention fraction shows that the annular stellar masses of the central galaxy beyond 10 kpc are less biased tracers of the most massive halos at intermediate redshifts than richness. This stratified fossil record originates mainly from the ex-situ phase of galaxy assembly. The outer stellar halo also traces the satellite population at intermediate redshift better than present-day richness. These results establish that the stellar profile of massive central galaxies encodes a radially stratified fossil record of halo assembly history.

entries.title: Long before plunge: Uncovering intermediate-mass black holes through their inspiralling compact object companions with LISA
entries.abstract: The Laser Interferometer Space Antenna (LISA) will provide novel capability to discover and study intermediate-mass (~$10^2-10^5 M_\odot$) black holes at the centres of dwarf galaxies and in dense stellar environments. We systematically map out the LISA-detectable parameter space of binaries consisting of a low-mass compact object spiralling into an intermediate-mass black hole (mass ratio ~$10^{-5} - 10^{-2}$) on equatorial orbits with generic eccentricity. The depth of the LISA survey reaches a redshift ~$5$ ($0.1$) for binaries with a primary black hole mass $m_1$ ~$10^4 M_\odot$ ($10^3 M_\odot$). If the orbital companion is a white dwarf, which could be disrupted prior to plunge, LISA's survey depth is well matched to (and, in many cases, exceeds) the one of electro-magnetic surveys. Although the maximum distance at which a source can be detected depends weakly on the orbital eccentricity, the latter strongly affects the portion of the binary inspiral over which a source is detectable. The instrument's sensitivity time-volume varies by many orders of magnitude depending on the binary's component masses: it reaches ~$1 - 10^3 Gpc^3 yr$ (~$10^{-2} - 10^3 Gpc^3 yr$) for the more massive systems with $m_1 = 10^5 M_\odot$ ($10^4 M_\odot$) and decreases to ~$10^{-4} - 1 Gpc^3 yr$ for lighter primary black holes with $m_1 = 10^3 M_\odot$. Importantly, from tens of percent to the overwhelming majority of the total sensitivity time-volume (and therefore number of potential detections) comes from sources that do not plunge during the yr-long mission lifetime and are observed at an earlier stage of their inspiral. Despite the poorly known merger rates of this class of sources, our results show that LISA could identify from a handful to ~$10^3$ intermediate-mass black holes providing a new observational avenue for studying these elusive objects and the environments in which they reside.

entries.title: Binary pulsar studies with multi-wavelength sky surveys. II. Companion star follow ups
entries.abstract: The identification of the stellar companions to binary pulsars and the extraction of the physical information encoded in their optical spectra are key to study the evolution of the binary system and how this is influenced by the interactions between the two stars. Obviously, extending the characterisation of the companion star spectra over an as large as possible wavelength range allows one to maximise the amount of information. In Paper I, we used 11 source catalogues built upon multi-wavelength (optical, infrared, ultraviolet) imaging sky surveys to search for the stellar companions of 144 field binary pulsars (i.e. not in Globular Clusters) selected from the Australia Telescope National Facility (ATNF) pulsar catalogue. For nine of these pulsars, for which the companion star had been already identified, we obtained new spectral information from imaging photometry in the surveys' bands. In particular, for some of these pulsars we provided the first possible detections of the companion star in either the ultraviolet or mid-infrared. Here, we serve this additional flux information as a base to update the spectral energy distribution (SED) of the companion stars and the multi-epoch catalogue photometry to look for flux modulation at the orbital period of the binary system.

entries.title: A Many-Shapes framework for Galactic Cosmic Rays
entries.abstract: Thanks to recent measurements by space and ground-level detectors, the energy spectra of cosmic ray protons and helium nuclei are now known with good precision over a broad energy range extending for more than six orders of magnitude, from a few GeV to approximately 10PeV. These measurements reveal that both spectra do not have a simple power--law form, and exhibit several features. The proton to helium ratio exhibits a very unexpected behavior: it decreases for rigidities $\lesssim 10^5$~GV, and increases for higher rigidities. Several authors have interpreted the observed spectral features as revealing the fact the CR spectra are formed by the contributions of a few components (in some cases as few as two) produced by sources that belong to distinct classes of astrophysical accelerators, with sources in the same class producing spectra with the same characteristic shape. Most of these authors also consider it necessary to include the contribution of one (or perhaps more than one) ``local'' sources, recently active in the vicinity of the solar system. However, this approach has several limitations, and in this work we discuss an alternative scenario in which the cosmic ray sources, even belonging to the same class, produce spectra with a broad range of shapes. The power--law form of the total source spectrum emerges as the average of these contributions. In this framework observable spectral features can be produced by statistical fluctuations, and different spectral slopes for protons and helium nuclei can be observed even if one assumes that acceleration is rigidity-dependent.

entries.title: Investigating the timescales traced by dynamical ages in young stellar systems
entries.abstract: Stars form in clustered environments, and then the stars may congregate into star clusters. The timescale on which individual stars form is not necessarily the same as the timescale on which star clusters assemble. Therefore, developing methods to probe these different timescales is a crucial part of understanding star cluster assembly and early evolution. Dynamical ages can be constructed from the kinematics of individual stars in clusters in the solar neighborhood using Gaia data. Using a star formation simulation, we test five different dynamical age methods. We divide dynamical ages into two approaches: methods which trace the size evolution of the cluster, and methods which trace the trajectories of individual stars. We confirm that size methods cannot accurately derive ages in bound clusters whereas methods tracing individual stars can be applied to both bound and unbound systems. We find that different dynamical age methods trace different epochs of star cluster formation and assembly: The method using stars with the oldest traceback ages provides an upper limit on stellar ages and the method using the median traceback ages is the best proxy for isochronal ages. Methods which trace the size evolution of the cluster best trace the onset of cluster expansion. Our work suggests that the median traceback time of stars moving away from the cluster provides the most reliable proxy for isochronal age, and that this method can be applied to any expanding system.

entries.title: The Edge of the Warm Corona in Active Galactic Nuclei
entries.abstract: A model of warm, dissipative corona on top of an accretion disk is investigated, to explain the soft X-ray excess (SXE) emission observed in active galactic nuclei (AGN). The final ray-traced spectrum, computed through photoionization code with Comptonization, accounts for both: emitted and reflected components. As a result, the strength of the SXE depends on the radial extend of the warm corona, i.e., its outer edge. We show that the radial transition from warm corona to disk atmosphere is governed by line cooling. By moving away from a central black hole Compton cooling is gradually replaced by line cooling, and the temperature drops sharply in vertical direction at a narrow iron ionization front, where iron ions Fe \textsc{xxv}--Fe \textsc{xxvi} recombine to Fe \textsc{xvii}. Notably, this transition takes place at a particular value of internal heating $\approx 1.6 \times 10^{-23}$ erg cm$^{3}$ s$^{-1}$, regardless of the Eddington ratio. We show, that at the given metal abundance, the SXE emitting area is larger for a higher accretion rate, in agreement with recent findings in changing look AGN. The overall emission spectrum from a warm corona is featureless, and the only iron K$_α$ line comes from a reflection. The line is stronger and more gravitationally distorted for a lower accretion rate, which is a direct result of the size of the warm corona. Furthermore, by increasing the iron abundance, the iron ionization front moves closer towards black hole, and a stronger iron line complex is emitted locally.

entries.title: Three-dimensional radiative transfer modeling of the scattering polarization in the solar H$α$ line
entries.abstract: The H$α$ line probes the solar chromosphere, but its scattering polarization is difficult to interpret because of magnetic fields, plasma motions, and atmospheric 3D inhomogeneities. We investigate its intensity and linear polarization in a 3D magnetohydrodynamic solar-atmosphere model including nonequilibrium hydrogen ionization. Using PORTA, we solve the full 3D non-LTE polarized radiative transfer problem for a multilevel hydrogen atom, accounting for atomic polarization, Hanle depolarization, horizontal radiative transfer, and macroscopic velocities. We degrade synthetic Stokes profiles to the spatial, spectral, and polarimetric resolution of ZIMPOL observations for direct comparison. The modeled center-to-limb variation follows the observed trend, with comparable polarization amplitudes. The profiles show large spatial variability from symmetry breaking by horizontal inhomogeneities and atmospheric dynamics, as well as diverse line-core asymmetries. Classifying $Q/I$ profiles by asymmetry reveals a statistical correlation between profile morphology and magnetic-field strength in the H$α$ formation region, consistent with Hanle depolarization: multi-peaked profiles favor stronger fields, whereas asymmetric single-peaked profiles favor weaker fields with smaller vertical strength variations. Thus, H$α$ scattering polarization reflects the interplay of magnetic fields, velocity gradients, and 3D radiative transfer. Our results highlight the need for 3D modeling to interpret H$α$ spectropolarimetry and its potential to diagnose chromospheric magnetism and dynamics.

entries.title: GRB 241030A: A fallback-accreting magnetar description of the early X-ray emission
entries.abstract: The bright, variable early X-ray emission of GRB~241030A at $z=1.411$ motivates investigating continued central-engine activity before the smoother afterglow emerges. We model a possible underlying magnetar contribution to the unabsorbed 0.3--10~keV XRT flux over 80--430~s, evolving the spin under fallback-disk and electromagnetic torques. A descriptive estimate gives $P_0\simeq4.25$~ms, $B\simeq3.04\times10^{15}$~G and source-frame $t_{\rm fb}\simeq143$~s, with exploratory temporal-block uncertainty ranges. The effective efficiency reaches its geometry-dependent ceiling of 81.2. At observer time 200~s, this realization has $P_*\simeq4.82$~ms and magnetospheric, corotation and light-cylinder radii $r_{\rm m}\simeq235$~km, $r_{\rm co}\simeq48$~km and $r_{\rm LC}\simeq230$~km. It is on the ejector branch; light-cylinder entry near 255~s initiates negative propeller torque and steepens the decline. The smooth component declines throughout the fitted interval; additional variable emission contributes to the observed maximum near 180~s. A correlated-residual Bayesian analysis permits a fainter component and broader dynamical histories, with median $P_0=16.8$~ms and central 68 per cent interval 2.76--286~ms. However, posterior predictive checks reveal that this statistical description typically underpredicts the observed flux level and variability, limiting its physical interpretation. Fallback-modified magnetar activity remains a possible descriptive scenario, but these analyses do not establish a unique underlying component or robust constraints on the initial spin and disk-interaction history. We also discuss Lense-Thirring precession and alternative mechanisms as possible origins of the early X-ray variability.

entries.title: The Cool Circumgalactic Echo of the Stellar-to-Halo Mass Relatio
entries.abstract: The stellar-to-halo mass relation (SHMR), a key prediction of galaxy formation models, peaks at $M_* \sim 3 \times 10^{10}\,M_\odot$. This scale is often attributed to circumgalactic baryonic feedback processes, however, direct observational evidence linking the two remains scarce. Using Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument (DESI) galaxy--quasar pairs, we map the cool circumgalactic medium (CGM) using Mg II $λ\lambda2796, 2803$ absorption with stacking technique across nearly three decades in stellar mass. The radial Mg II absorption equivalent-width profile, $W_{\rm MgII} \propto D^k$, becomes progressively shallower with increasing stellar mass, following $k = 0.70\log(M_*/M_\odot)-9.12$. Crucially, we find that the $W_{\rm MgII}$ in the CGM scales tightly with the SHMR. The $W_{\rm MgII}$ peaks at the same characteristic mass as the SHMR, coinciding with a transition of the cool CGM from super-virial to sub-virial kinematics. Low-mass halos show excess non-gravitational motions consistent with recycled accretion and feedback-driven circulation, whereas massive halos show halo-centric heating that may maintain star formation quenching. This study bridges the gap between cool CGM and SHMR, showing that peak star formation efficiency coincides with the most abundant cool CGM reservoirs.

entries.title: NS 1987A: A Potential Probe of Crustal Superfluidity with Future X-ray Observations
entries.abstract: Several indirect observations imply that the central compact object in the supernova SN 1987A is likely to be the youngest neutron star identified to date, NS 1987A. We investigate how a future detection of its thermal X-ray emission could constrain neutron-star interiors, using cooling models and a generic high-resolution, large-area X-ray observatory with \textit{Lynx}-like capabilities as a sensitivity benchmark. For the adopted sensitivity and observing window, NS 1987A is detectable at $t\sim60~{\rm yr}$ (roughly 2047) unless rapid neutrino cooling operates, such as the direct Urca process. If the neutron superfluidity in the inner crust is weak, the temperature profile inside NS 1987A is likely not to be isothermal at the detection. In that case, the future direct observation of NS 1987A is a potential probe of the properties inside the inner crust. We compare alternative X-ray observatories and emphasize that both effective area and angular resolution, needed to reduce contamination from the surrounding remnant, determine whether this diagnostic can be realized.

entries.title: Numerical-Relativity Particle-in-Cell Simulations: Self-Gravitating Collisionless Matter in Dynamical Spacetimes
entries.abstract: Gravitational collapse and instability, black-hole dynamics in systems with large scale separations, and questions surrounding extremal black hole formation require full nonlinear studies using accurate and adapted numerical tools. To this end, we present a new algorithm to study collisionless relativistic systems using a fully kinetic description of matter coupled to the evolving spacetime. In detail, we present a numerical-relativity particle-in-cell (NRPIC) framework for solving the Einstein--Vlasov system in three spatial dimensions. Implemented on top of the performance-portable \texttt{AthenaK} code, the method couples particle dynamics to Z4c spacetime evolution in moving puncture gauge through conservative stress-energy deposition on adaptively refined meshes. Our implementation makes use of advances in the computational modeling of relativistic plasmas using modern PIC models, now made available to general-relativistic gravity via an equivalent electrodynamic formulation. We introduce a Boris-type particle pusher that exploits the electrodynamic (Lorentz force) form of the geodesic force. We validate the coupled evolution against spherical dust collapse, follow prolate collapse through collisionless caustics into black-hole formation, and investigate the stability and nonlinear migration of relativistic clusters. Highlighting its potential to study gravitational instability in NR, we simulate the collapse of two overdensities within a common collisionless envelope, following black-hole formation, binary inspiral and merger, and subsequent mass accretion onto the remnant.

entries.title: Joint Gaia-Hipparcos astrometry, RV, and Imaging posteriors from the G23H Hipparcos sample
entries.abstract: We present uniform posteriors indicating the presence or absence of stellar and planetary companions over a sample of $10^5$ stars in Hipparcos and Gaia. We use the "G23H" catalog to fit a model that incorporates absolute astrometry constraints from Hipparcos, Gaia DR2, and Gaia DR3, as well as Gaia DR3 photometry, excess RV variability, and includes information from the presence or absence of common-proper motion companions. The resulting posteriors can be used directly to detect new companions, to target RV and imaging follow-up observations, and for downstream demographics studies. We highlight example detections of known and new candidate companions and the companion detection rate across the HR diagram. The modelling approach we present is directly applicable to Gaia DR4 epoch astrometry and RVs. All posteriors are provided as a machine-readable catalog and user-accessible website http://exopo.st/.

entries.title: AGN Feedback Turbulence in Cool-core Clusters: Evidence from XRISM
entries.abstract: The XRISM X-ray Observatory has revealed evidence for a "double-cascade" scenario in the Perseus cluster, in which active galactic nucleus (AGN) feedback and mergers drive turbulence over distinct radial ranges and spatial scales. Whether this gas kinematic feature is common among cool-core clusters remains unclear. Here, we revisit XRISM observations of A1795 and A2029 to investigate the signatures of AGN feedback and their contribution to the gas velocity fields. In A1795, AGN feedback dominates the velocity dispersion in the core, similar to Perseus, and may provide turbulent heating at a rate comparable to radiative cooling. In contrast, we obtain only an upper limit on the AGN feedback contribution in A2029, where merger-driven motions dominate. Tailored simulations indicate that an off-axis minor merger $\simeq1.6$ Gyr ago displaced the central low-entropy gas in A2029, potentially suppressing AGN activity. This gas is now returning to the center, possibly facilitating the re-establishment of AGN feedback. We propose an evolutionary view of the double-cascade scenario, in which merger-driven motions dominate during and shortly after significant mergers, while feedback-driven turbulence re-emerges in cluster cores as systems relax. This framework provides a basis for interpreting XRISM kinematic measurements of (weak) cool-core clusters. Our findings highlight the importance of spatially resolved gas kinematics and detailed modeling for identifying double-cascade features and disentangling the contributions of AGN feedback and mergers.

entries.title: Forward modeling linear variable filter data: High resolution PAH and Paschen-$α$ maps from SPHEREx
entries.abstract: Polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbon (PAH) emission is a powerful tool for the study of the interstellar medium (ISM) in both Galactic and extragalactic contexts. It can reveal ionization state, radiation field, metallicity, composition, and ISM structure as sculpted by processes like turbulence and stellar feedback. Here we use NASA's SPHEREx to produce clean, high-resolution PAH maps at spectral resolution R $\sim$ 35 (compared to WISE at R $\sim$ 2). Prior treatments of the SPHEREx linear variable filter data seek to convert them to more conventional band-averaged maps that can leave striping artifacts associated with spatially variable wavelength sampling, especially at emission lines. In contrast, we deliver a scalable forward-modeling method capable of generating high-quality all-sky SPHEREx emission-line maps at 8.5 arcsec FWHM angular resolution (on 6.4 arcsec pixels), while naturally producing maps without visible striping. We reformat the data into a pixel-level database, mask stellar contamination, and infill missing pixels with a conditional, data-driven, anisotropic Gaussian process. We apply our method to produce 3.3 $μ$m and 3.4 $μ$m PAH and Paschen-$α$ emission maps of a set of fields spanning a range of Galactic and extragalactic conditions including the Rosette nebula, the Corona Australis molecular cloud, M33, and M31. We demonstrate the quality and synergies of our SPHEREx 3.3 $μ$m PAH maps by comparisons with other available gas and dust tracer maps and achieve sensitivities up to $σ(I_{3.3}) = 2.7 \times 10^{-8}$ erg s$^{-1}$ cm$^{-2}$ sr$^{-1}$. We estimate that a two-year extension of the SPHEREx survey, with modest modifications to the scanning strategy, would match or exceed the PAH sensitivity of WISE over the whole sky.

entries.title: Search for a Dispersion Measure Excess Toward Nearby Galaxy Halos Using Fast Radio Bursts from the Second CHIME/FRB Baseband Catalog
entries.abstract: Fast radio bursts (FRBs) probe foreground ionized baryons via their dispersion measures (DM). Using 1748 sub-arcminute-localized sources from the Second CHIME/FRB Baseband Catalog, we conduct a statistical stacking study of the circumgalactic media (CGM) of nearby galaxies by analyzing the DMs of FRBs whose sightlines intersect foreground halos. For galaxy halos within 50 Mpc, we measure a mean DM excess of $119\pm44$ pc~cm$^{-3}$ $(p = 0.0053; \sim 2.6σ)$ within one virial radius. Expanding to 150 Mpc (628 intersections), we find a tentative decline in the mean DM as a function of impact parameter $(p = 0.0046; \sim 2.6σ)$, which is predominantly driven by typical Milky Way (MW)-like galaxies $(10 \leq \log(M_*/M_\odot)\leq 11)$. We use this DM profile to constrain parameters of the CGM electron density distribution, $n_e^\mathrm{CGM}(r) \propto r^{-3β}$, finding an extrapolated central electron density in the range of $(1.7-21.1) \times 10^{-3}\mathrm{\,cm}^{-3}$, with a radial power-law index of $β= 0.68^{+0.15}_{-0.16}$, consistent with constraints from X-ray stacking studies of MW-like galaxies. At very low impact parameters, we detect a significant DM deficit likely due to cross-matching FRBs that originate from galaxies within our galaxy sample. By deriving the DM-galaxy cross-correlation function, we show that this deficit matches theoretical predictions if 20 FRBs originate from galaxies within 150 Mpc, indicating that CHIME/FRB detects a higher fraction of low-$z$ FRBs than previously thought. We forecast that $10^4$ FRBs with similar localization errors will provide a 5-$σ$ detection of the CGM, and that FRBs at intermediate redshifts ($0.4\lesssim z_\mathrm{FRB}\lesssim 0.75$) are ideal for studying intervening CGMs.

entries.title: The Brown Dwarf Desert is a Mass-Ratio Desert: Astrometric Demographics of 63,254 Stars
entries.abstract: Brown dwarfs are rare as close companions to stars compared to planets and stellar companions, a paucity known as the brown dwarf desert. Whether the desert sits at a fixed companion mass or a fixed companion-to-star mass-ratio $q$ has been difficult to test, because microlensing, radial velocities, and direct imaging have sampled comparatively narrow slices of stellar mass and separation. Here we apply a novel joint-modelling method to Hipparcos and Gaia DR2/DR3 astrometry from 63,254 stars to complete this picture with a sample 1-2 orders of magnitude larger than those of previous wide-orbit demographic studies. For the first time, we present a single survey that measures occurrence rates of both planetary and stellar companions on 3--94 yr orbits ($\sim$2--20\,au) across host masses from M dwarfs to B stars. We find that the desert is a mass-ratio feature: companions are strongly depleted at $q\approx2\%$ independent of stellar mass from M to B stars, and a desert at fixed companion mass is excluded. Furthermore, we find a positive trend in occurrence with metallicity below the mass-ratio desert, but a negative trend above. The desert therefore separates two distinct populations, plausibly two formation channels, that each scale with stellar mass: the lightest stellar-like companions of K stars ($\sim13 \, M_{jup}$) are less massive than the heaviest planet-like companions of B stars ($\sim27, M_{jup}$), which continue well beyond the deuterium-burning limit. Mass-ratio, not mass, is therefore the physically meaningful boundary between planets and their stellar-like counterparts.

analysis.reason: This ZTF spectroscopic census of hydrogen-rich SLSNe directly constrains circumstellar interaction, pre-explosion mass loss, and possible Ia-CSM contamination, which are central to supernova-engine and CSM studies.
analysis.result: Of 106 hydrogen-rich SLSNe, 105 show narrow Balmer emission and are spectroscopically SLSNe-IIn; SN 2022lvm is the sole broad-lined SLSN-II in the discussed 2021–2022 subset comparison (1/36, 2.8%). Measured $L_{\mathrm{H}\alpha}$ spans $2.2\times10^{40}$ to $1.5\times10^{42}\,\mathrm{erg\,s^{-1}}$ (median $2.6\times10^{41}\,\mathrm{erg\,s^{-1}}$). The median Balmer decrement rises from 2.85 before $+100$ d to 4.40 afterward, below the Ia-CSM comparison medians 6.58 and 17.76. After excluding the SLSN-II and six Ia-CSM-like objects, median shell speed correlates with peak magnitude ($r=0.63$, $p=0.010$): brighter events tend to have lower $v_{\rm s}$. For 13 calibrated objects at $v_{\rm CSM}=100\,\mathrm{km\,s^{-1}}$ and $\epsilon=0.5$, $\dot{M}\sim0.028$–$0.30\,M_{\odot}\,\mathrm{yr^{-1}}$ from $L=\frac{1}{2}\epsilon\dot{M}v_{\rm s}^{3}/u_{\rm w}$. Six of 105 narrow-line events ($\sim6\%$) are Ia-CSM-like. Narrow interaction lines can persist beyond $+200$ d, with no Balmer morphology unique to SLSNe-IIn relative to fainter SNe IIn.
analysis.problem: Whether luminous narrow-line SLSNe-IIn are spectroscopically only the bright extreme of SNe IIn, what dense hydrogen-rich CSM and enhanced pre-explosion mass loss they require, and whether narrow Balmer lines plus high luminosity uniquely imply core collapse rather than Ia-CSM.
analysis.method: The study uses 304 optical spectra of 106 ZTF events selected at rest-frame peak $M\leq-19.9$ mag, with phases $(t-t_{\rm peak})/(1+z)$ and fluxes scaled by $10^{-0.4(m_{\rm GP}-m_{\rm syn})}$ from Gaussian-process light curves (287 absolutely calibrated). Balmer luminosity, pEW and FWHM are measured after local continuum subtraction. Single-epoch Monte Carlo electron-scattering snapshots (escatter; $10^{5}$ H$\alpha$ photons outside a cold dense shell) fit line profiles. Mass-loss rates use $L=\frac{1}{2}\epsilon\dot{M}\frac{v_{\rm s}^{3}}{u_{\rm w}}$ and $\dot{M}=\frac{2L}{\epsilon}\frac{u_{\rm w}}{v_{\rm s}^{3}}$, with luminosity integrated from the spectra and a blackbody extension to 3000–20000 Å.
assumptions: Quoted mass-loss rates use the adopted CSM-interaction model with $\epsilon=0.5$ and $v_{\rm CSM}=100\,\mathrm{km\,s^{-1}}$, commonly with a shock speed of $5000\,\mathrm{km\,s^{-1}}$.
limits: Inferred mass-loss rates are order-of-magnitude estimates rather than precise progenitor mass-loss histories.

The SNR downstream is split into independent shells with adiabatic losses, and the $pp$ gamma-ray flux is integrated with Naima and Kafexhiu cross sections, comparing cases with and without stochastic acceleration and wave feedback.

For $0.034\le\kappa_e\le0.060$, successive maxima of $P_z$ period-double eight times toward a stable $256$-cycle, with spacing ratios approaching $\delta_{\rm F}\simeq4.669$. At $\kappa_e=0.055025$ the leading Lyapunov estimate is $\widehat\lambda_1\simeq2.8\times10^{-3}$ for bounded irregular evolution. At $-1.05^{\circ}<l<0.55^{\circ}$, observed $\mathrm{HR}\gtrsim 0.3$ exceeds $\mathrm{HR}<0.2$ predicted for $5\times10^{22}<N_{\rm H}<8\times10^{22}\,\mathrm{cm}^{-2}$. Scale heights are $h_{l,\rm s}=2^{\circ}$ ($\sim280\,\mathrm{pc}$), $h_{b,\rm s}=0.31^{\circ}$ ($\sim44\,\mathrm{pc}$), $h_{l,\rm h}=0.66^{\circ}$ ($\sim90\,\mathrm{pc}$), and $h_{b,\rm h}=0.17^{\circ}$ ($\sim24\,\mathrm{pc}$). analysis.reason: This directly constrains the circumgalactic contribution to FRB dispersion measure using the second CHIME/FRB baseband catalog, including a radial and mass-dependent DM stack relevant to FRB sightline environments.
analysis.result: Within $D_L\le50\,\mathrm{Mpc}$ and one virial radius, the mean excess is $119\pm44\,\mathrm{pc\,cm^{-3}}$ ($p=0.0053$, about $2.6\sigma$). Across 628 intersections to $150\,\mathrm{Mpc}$, mean DM tentatively declines with impact parameter ($p=0.0046$, about $2.6\sigma$), mainly for $10\le\log(M_*/M_\odot)\le11$. The adopted CGM scaling is $n_e^{\mathrm{CGM}}(r)\propto r^{-3\beta}$, with extrapolated $n_{e,0}=(1.7-21.1)\times10^{-3}\,\mathrm{cm^{-3}}$ and $\beta=0.68^{+0.15}_{-0.16}$. The excess peaks near $\sim90\pm75\,\mathrm{pc\,cm^{-3}}$ at $0.2\lesssim b_{\min}/r_{\rm CGM}\lesssim0.4$, whereas large-scale structure contributes only about $14\pm39\,\mathrm{pc\,cm^{-3}}$.
analysis.problem: The paper tests whether foreground galaxy CGM halos produce an extragalactic FRB DM excess and whether its radial behavior traces CGM baryons rather than large-scale structure or host-galaxy cross-matching.
analysis.method: BaseCat2 contains 2086 bursts and 1748 independent sources, stacked on foreground halos using $\mathrm{DM}=\int_0^z n_e(z')(1+z')^{-1}dl$ and $\Delta\mathrm{DM}_{\mathrm{egal}}=\mathrm{DM}-\mathrm{DM}_{\mathrm{MW}}$. The radial analysis uses $b_{\min}/r_{\rm CGM}$, Gaussian bin-membership weights, and the fit $n_e^{\rm CGM}(r)=n_{e,0}[1+(r/r_c)^2]^{-3\beta/2}$. SLOW and Simba comparisons test alternative contributions, while $\eta_{\mathrm{CGM}}=\mathrm{DM}_{\mathrm{CGM}}/\mathrm{DM}_{\mathrm{cosmic}}$ forecasts favorable redshifts.
assumptions: Because DM_CGM and DM_cosmic are drawn from different simulations, they are treated as statistically independent.
limits: The low-impact-parameter extragalactic-DM deficit is likely contaminated by matching FRBs to their own host galaxies.

analysis.research_progress: The work advances CGM studies from small FRB stacks to a baseband sample with a $\sim2.6\sigma$ excess of $119\pm44\,\mathrm{pc\,cm^{-3}}$ and a tentative $b_{\min}/r_{\rm CGM}$ decline. It also identifies $0.4\lesssim z_{\mathrm{FRB}}\lesssim0.75$ as favorable and forecasts that about $10^4$ baseband FRBs can reach $\sim5\sigma$, especially for $\log(M_*/M_\odot)>10$.
